item.title: Three recommended for 3rd District judgeship
item.description: The Commission on Judicial Selection recommends John Brooks, Holli Mayer, and Sarah Palm for the 3rd Judicial District judgeship in Minnesota.

item.title: Judge orders secrecy for report on Trump classified-documents case
item.description: A Florida federal judge blocked the public release of special counsel Jack Smith's report on Trump's classified documents case, citing grand jury secrecy and presumption of innocence.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court to hear bid by oil companies to toss climate suits
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear ExxonMobil and Suncor's appeal to dismiss a Boulder, Colorado, climate change lawsuit seeking damages for fossil fuel impacts.

item.title: Low bids drop cost of Stearns County justice center
item.description: Stearns County’s new $290M justice center in St. Cloud draws 225 bids, many local, as construction nears and environmental review moves ahead.

item.title: Federal Circuit upholds $42M Christmas tree patent verdict
item.description: The Federal Circuit affirmed a record $42.4M Minnesota patent verdict for Willis Electric, rejecting Polygroup’s appeal over artificial Christmas trees.

item.title: Former Trump attorney seeks recusal of Wisconsin justices in fake electors case
item.description: Former Trump campaign attorney Jim Troupis seeks to recuse Wisconsin Supreme Court justices from his forgery case involving fake electors in the 2020 election.

item.title: Supreme Court wades into Line 5 venue dispute between Michigan, Enbridge
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments on whether Enbridge can remove Michigan's Line 5 pipeline case to federal court despite missing the 30-day removal deadline.

item.title: 8th Circuit reverses Minnesota design defect verdict in aerosol duster case
item.description: The 8th U.S. Circuit Court reversed a Minnesota jury verdict, ruling no evidence showed CRC's aerosol duster was unreasonably dangerous.

item.title: Somali day cares sue state, allege biased investigations
item.description: Somali-owned day care centers in Minnesota sue state agency, alleging ethnic bias and due process violations over CCAP payment suspensions and investigations.

item.title: Former federal prosecutor Slaughter rejoins Robins Kaplan
item.description: Former federal prosecutor Allen Slaughter has rejoined Robins Kaplan LLP in Minnesota, focusing on civil rights and complex litigation matters.
